review_notes: All three articles locate the Mauwasi bridge blockage on Friday morning, Aug 25; Aug 26 is the subsequent report date.

Besinda/Silichong is the 2020 monsoon landslide, not 2022. Retrospective says Asar 27 night (Jul 11); contemporary Republica and Kathmandu Post accounts identify the destructive slide around 2 am Sunday Jul 12, so use the physical calendar date.
Original Himalayan Times article and contemporaneous Kathmandu Post report place the Shantipur, Gulmi landslide on Tuesday night Sep 20; Sep 21 is publication day.
Jairigad hydropower canal serving Dunai is in Dolpa; the Sep 6 report says the landslide swept the canal away Tuesday Sep 4. Jajarkot is the dateline, not event district.

The January 2021 articles retrospectively describe the fatal Lidi, Jugal landslide (39 eventual deaths), not a Jan 2021 event; contemporaneous Aug 14 reports confirm that date. Sources describe a landslide, not a separately evidenced debris flow.
Nagarik identifies a Friday landslide burying Yam Bahadur Shris as he repaired a field canal at Kaligandaki-4 Phurse; Friday was Jul 10, not Jul 9.
Bajura Barjugad obstruction followed rain from Monday night; a separate Jul 28 contemporary report explicitly says the landslide fell Tuesday morning. Jul 27 is the rain-onset date, not the slide.
Setopati published Aug 19 and reports a 2:30 am fatal landslide while Bishnu Prasad Lamichhane cleared debris at Belkotgadhi-5 Lamachaur; one person died.
Tuin Khola landslide blocked the Narayangadh-Muglin road at 7:25 pm Jul 13; the site is in Chitwan, not Kathmandu.
Sep 10 Ujyaalo report places the road-blocking Raduwa slide at Ganyapdhura-2, Dadeldhura, with the highway closed since the previous night (Sep 9); Achham is another district served by the road.
Both Aug 31 articles report the Kerabari, Bharatpur-29 mud-laden slide blocked Narayangadh-Muglin road from approximately 2:30 am that day.

The retrospective Aug 31 story identifies Barla Churkhola, Panchdeval Binayak-8 in Achham (Doti is dateline). Slide struck about 3 am after Thursday night, i.e. Friday Aug 29; Kavita and Nim Joshi died.
Feb 4 Ujyaalo article says the dry slide above the road at Hedangna, Makalu-3 occurred the previous evening and blocked Khadbari-Kimathanka road; this record describes a road obstruction.
OnlineKhabar reports the new obstruction at bridge no. 3 on Narayangadh-Muglin road from Thursday Jun 29 about 1:30 pm. Kathmandu is only the story dateline.

Ramtola is a continuing slope failure, not a Sep 12 onset. A later detailed follow-up specifies Sep 5 cracking, Sep 6 substantial movement, and the major damaging slide taking water tanks Sep 7 (Bhadra 22); use Sep 7 for the described major physical event.
Nepal Press states a landslide buried a livestock shed in Shitganga-13, Arghakhanchi, killing Bishnu Thapa; Rupandehi is the dateline.
Ratopati states the Mar 29 evening slide at Bakhor, Rong-4, Ilam obstructed Mechi Highway and police explicitly reported no casualties; Jhapa is the dateline.
Setopati Aug 4 says the new Ghumaune, Bharatpur-29 road-blocking slide occurred at 6 am that morning; Aug 2 was a distinct earlier slide at the same site.
Himalayan Times explicitly locates the Oct 11 Piple BP Highway obstruction in Roshi Rural Municipality-11, Kavrepalanchok; Kathmandu is its dateline.

The RSS copy is datelined Gulmi Sep 28 and says the Bishnupanjar slide obstructed the road since "last night"; this places the reported physical fall on Sep 27, not the Sep 28 dateline or Sep 29 site posting.
Setopati names Kalekhola, Shubha Kalika Rural Municipality-1 in Kalikot as the landslide site and says Karnali Highway blocked from 11 am Aug 24; Surkhet is a travel/treatment destination.
Ujyaalo published Jul 17 and explicitly says the slide injuring four people in Kuse-8 Dallena fell around 8 pm the previous night. Nov 2, 2024 is unrelated to this landslide.
Setopati states the Simaltal slide at Bharatpur-29, Chitwan, swept two buses into Trishuli at approximately 3:30 am Jul 12; Kathmandu was not the event district.

The Oct 2 follow-up places the Temal-2 slope collapse at about 11 am on Asoj 11 (Sep 27), after rain began Asoj 10; six relatives' bodies recovered and two remain missing, so do not count eight confirmed deaths.
